title: A saturated solution is a dynamic equilibrium
caption: In a saturated AgCl solution, ions leave the solid as fast as they rejoin it: AgCl(s) ⇌ Ag⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq). Ksp = [Ag⁺][Cl⁻] = 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁰ mol² dm⁻⁶ at 25 °C, so very few ions are in solution.
alt: A beaker with a layer of solid silver chloride on the bottom and a few silver and chloride ions in the solution above.
description: Solid AgCl at the bottom, a lattice of Ag⁺ and Cl⁻.
Only a few Ag⁺ and Cl⁻ ions dissolved in the water above, in equal numbers.
